headline: The medication that sounded like 'isiziromycin' was not recommended for Mr. Fleming's strep throat because it can interact with his Risperdal, so clindamycin was prescribed instead, and its dose still needs confirming.

followUps.title: Confirm the clindamycin dose
followUps.detail: The recording gives two different amounts. One time it says 300 milligrams, three times a day for 10 days. Another time it says 500 milligrams, 300 milligrams, three times for 10 days. The recording does not show which is right. Ask the pharmacist or doctor to confirm which is correct.

followUps.title: Check the antibiotic name in the recording
followUps.detail: The name was heard differently in different parts of the recording, and the recording may be wrong. Listen to the part from about 0:32 and the part from about 3:36 to 4:08. Confirm the name with your care team.

followUps.title: Pick up the clindamycin prescription
followUps.detail: The pharmacist said they would prepare it for Mr. Fleming, counsel him, and follow up with him. The recording does not give a pickup time. Ask the pharmacy when it will be ready.

instructions.text: Do not take the medication that sounded like 'isiziromycin' for this strep throat. The clinician said it can interact with Risperdal and cause an increase in QT prolongation, which can lead to death.
Take clindamycin three times a day for 10 days, once the dose is confirmed.

openQuestions.text: Which clindamycin amount is right? The recording gives 300 milligrams, and also 500 milligrams with 300 milligrams.
Some allergy details are unclear in the recording. It mentions penicillin and a cephalosporin-type antibiotic, but the reaction and the second drug name were garbled.
